items.title: Milt Fillius interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 18, 2000
items.q: And most of the black guys I know, Terry and Sweets Edison and people like that — you just never get on that subject. You know that they like you. You know that you’re their friend

ctx.x: Did you find the same type of feeling in the other fellas of that era that you got to know like Milt Hinton?

Well I think so but I don’t know him that well. Milt Hinton I’m pretty sure is broad minded about anything. But he is from an era where you don’t display your feelings. And most of the black guys I know, Terry and Sweets Edison and people like that — you just never get on that subject. You know that they like you. You know that you’re their friend and that there’s no color bar between you. But I don’t think you ever get far enough in their innermost thoughts to know what they think. Milt Hinton for example. His…
Yeah, they attract — people want to be near them.
